# Findings

*Generated by `scripts/analyze.py --findings`. Every number is queried from the marks panel at run time; nothing here is typed by hand.*

Four measurements over **5,479 marks**, after the guards below. In one line each:

1. **Marks move more often than expected.** 75.0% of consecutive observations change — `plan.md` expected 60–70%.
2. **Managers on the same date disagree by a median of 10.8%**, and 92 of 130 same-date groups contain more than one price level, so most disagreement is about *which round is reflected*, not about what a round is worth.
3. **A new price level reaches half its eventual holders in a median of 30 days** and all of them in 90.
4. **The Cerebras event study cannot be run from this data**, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight. See §4.

---

## The guards, and what they cost

Three rules from `plan.md` are applied before any measurement, in one place so that no measurement can forget one.

| | marks |
|---|---|
| In the panel | 5,479 |
| Excluded: no price | 294 |
| Excluded: blocked from change series | 301 |
| — of which confirmed splits awaiting adjustment | 7 |
| — of which unadjudicated suspected splits | 0 |
| Excluded: on an incomplete run | 0 |

The incomplete-run guard is **currently inert**: there are 0 incomplete runs, so it removed nothing. It is worth saying that rather than implying the guard did work.

**A zero delta and a carry-forward are not distinguishable from a filing.** A fund that re-valued and arrived at the same number looks exactly like one that carried the old number forward. So this report says *unchanged* and never says *stale*.

## 1. Re-mark versus carry-forward

`plan.md`: *"30-40% of consecutive observations unchanged"*

| | steps |
|---|---|
| Consecutive observations | 4,079 |
| Moved | 3,060 (75.0%) |
| Unchanged | 1,019 (25.0%) |
| First observation, no prior | 1,099 |

**25.0% unchanged, against an expected 30–40%.** Marks move more often than the plan assumed, so staleness is even less of a problem than the thesis allowed for.

The result does not rest on rounding:

| treating as unchanged | share |
|---|---|
| exactly equal (the rule used) | 25.0% |
| any move under 0.1% | 26.3% |
| any move under 1% | 29.6% |

Even the most generous reading stays below the plan's band.

### It varies enormously by company

| company | steps | moved | unchanged | managers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Databricks, Inc. | 1,812 | 1,453 | 359 (19.8%) | 28 |
| Space Exploration Technologies Corp. | 1,259 | 788 | 471 (37.4%) | 12 |
| Anduril Industries, Inc. | 389 | 296 | 93 (23.9%) | 8 |
| Anthropic PBC | 271 | 265 | 6 (2.2%) | 12 |
| X.AI Corp | 171 | 88 | 83 (48.5%) | 8 |
| OpenAI Group PBC | 95 | 94 | 1 (1.1%) | 12 |
| Cerebras Systems Inc. | 42 | 40 | 2 (4.8%) | 3 |
| Figure AI Inc. | 19 | 17 | 2 (10.5%) | 2 |
| Groq, Inc. | 11 | 11 | 0 (0.0%) | 3 |

Anthropic and OpenAI are re-marked at almost every observation; X.AI and SpaceX are carried forward between a third and a half of the time. A single headline rate for "private marks" would hide that.

## 2. Cross-manager dispersion

`plan.md`: *"Databricks ~9% spread, Perplexity ~19%"* — and its framing: *"the interesting question is not 'do funds disagree about value' — they mostly don't."*

Measured two ways, because they answer different questions.

**Same date, no window** — 130 groups of at least 3 managers marking one company and class kind on the *same* period end. Nothing can drift in.

| | |
|---|---|
| Median spread | **10.82%** |
| 90th percentile | 40.5% |
| Widest | 111.9% |
| Groups agreeing within 1% | 35 of 130 |
| Groups containing more than one price level | 92 |

So funds **do** disagree on the same date, by about 11% at the median — but 92 of 130 of those groups contain two or more distinct price levels, which means the disagreement is usually *which round has been reflected yet*, not what the round was worth. That is propagation seen side-on, and it is measured directly in §3.

The widest same-date groups:

| company | kind | date | managers | range | spread | levels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Databricks, Inc. | common | 2022-12-31 | 5 | 28.32–60.0 | 111.9% | 3 |
| Databricks, Inc. | common | 2023-03-31 | 6 | 31.49–60.0 | 90.5% | 3 |
| Databricks, Inc. | common | 2023-06-30 | 6 | 39.54–73.16 | 85.0% | 4 |
| Space Exploration Technologies Corp. | preferred | 2026-03-31 | 4 | 2896.245–5265.9 | 81.8% | 2 |
| Anthropic PBC | preferred | 2025-12-31 | 5 | 140.9676–254.43 | 80.5% | 3 |
| Databricks, Inc. | preferred | 2023-07-31 | 4 | 50.9–91.6909 | 80.1% | 4 |
| X.AI Corp | preferred | 2025-03-31 | 3 | 21.65–36.56 | 68.9% | 2 |
| Anduril Industries, Inc. | preferred | 2025-12-31 | 5 | 40.8828–62.0 | 51.6% | 5 |

**Within a 31-day window** the picture is dominated by rounds in flight: 180 of 237 windows (75.9%) contain more than one price level.

### Two things deliberately not claimed

- **Within-level agreement is not reported as a finding.** Prices inside a level agree to within 2.0% because that is the clustering threshold. Quoting it would restate a definition.
- **Two scale artifacts were set aside** rather than averaged in, and named here:

None survived into the windows reported above, because comparing within class kind already separates SpaceX's common from its preferred.

The two that forced this design:

- **SpaceX files preferred at ten times common by convention** — 81.00 against 970.00 on the same day. An earlier version of this measurement compared them and reported a 1,098% "spread".
- **One Coatue mark of `OPENAI GLOBAL, LLC`** carries 150,000,000 units at $1.5072. A hundred and fifty million shares of a company marked near $500 is an LLC interest priced per dollar of commitment. It produced a 31,983% "spread" before it was caught, and it is the `$1.00 OpenAI` open issue, now pinned to one row.

## 3. Propagation lag

How long a new price level takes to reach the managers who eventually adopt it, over 37 events with at least 3 adopters.

| | days |
|---|---|
| Median, first manager to **half** the adopters | **30** |
| Worst, to half | 92 |
| Median, first to **last** adopter | 90 |
| Worst, to last | 427 |

The biggest events, by how many managers adopted the level:

| company | level | managers | to half | to all | first seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Databricks, Inc. | 190.0000 | 20 | 0d | 90d | 2025-12-31 |
| Databricks, Inc. | 190.1000 | 20 | 0d | 90d | 2025-12-31 |
| Databricks, Inc. | 92.5000 | 18 | 31d | 151d | 2024-11-30 |
| Databricks, Inc. | 150.0000 | 16 | 30d | 61d | 2025-08-31 |
| Databricks, Inc. | 73.4416 | 13 | 30d | 396d | 2023-08-31 |
| Databricks, Inc. | 73.5000 | 13 | 30d | 396d | 2023-08-31 |
| OpenAI Group PBC | 687.6869 | 12 | 0d | 30d | 2026-03-31 |
| Anthropic PBC | 259.0082 | 10 | 27d | 89d | 2026-01-31 |

**A round reaches half its holders within about a month and effectively all of them within a quarter.** For the largest events — Databricks at 190.00 across 20 managers, OpenAI at 687.6869 across 12 — half the managers report the new level on the *same period end*, which is a lag of zero.

Why first-to-last is the weaker number: Two bounds, both real. The lag cannot be shorter than the fiscal-quarter stagger -- a manager reporting on 30 April cannot reflect a 31 March repricing any sooner -- so this measures observability, not diligence. And first-to-last includes managers still carrying an old level long after the company repriced, which is staleness rather than slow propagation; that is why the headline is first-to-half.

The stagger that makes any of this visible: 55 distinct period ends across 2022-11-30 to 2026-04-30, clustering on 5 days of the month.

## 4. The Cerebras study, and why it cannot be run

`plan.md`: *"Level 3 at 89.02 on 2026-03-31 against Level 1 at 236.99 on 2026-05-29"*, described as *"a free, clean, private-mark-to-public-price event study with no additional data collection"*.

**It is not free, because the Level 1 observation is not in the data.** Two independent reasons:

1. the private layer is filtered to FAIR_VALUE_LEVEL = 3, so Level 1 rows never entered Postgres: all 5,806 raw_holdings rows are Level 3
2. the bulk archive's newest period end is 2026-04-30; plan.md's Level 1 observation has a 2026-05-29 period end, which is in unpublished 2026Q3

Probing the raw 2026Q2 archive with no fair-value filter returns 22 Cerebras row groups, all Level 3. The earliest possible Level 1 period end is therefore after the archive ends. The same probe on 2026Q1 returns 10 groups, also all Level 3.

Either reason alone would be surmountable — the first is a filter to widen, the second a quarter to wait for. Together they mean the comparison needs the live-EDGAR path, which is Week 3's still-open item.

From 21.4600 at 2022-12-31 to 100.2600 at 2026-04-30 — a 367.2% gain over the window, with the last two observations stepping 89.02 → 100.26.

`plan.md`'s Level 1 figure of $236.99 would imply the private marks sat far below the eventual public price. **This report does not make that claim**, because the $236.99 observation is not in any data this project has ingested, and a comparison against a number taken from the plan document rather than from a filing would be a finding with no provenance.

## 5. The event study, built and waiting

The Cerebras comparison needs one thing this project does not have: a Level 1 observation. Everything else is now in place, so that the study runs the day the archive catches up rather than being rebuilt from memory months later.

**What was built**

| | |
|---|---|
| `public_observations` | a separate table for universe-company holdings at any fair value level other than 3 |
| `src/ingest/public_marks.py` | scans the raw zips for them, because the Parquet layer was itself built with the Level 3 filter and cannot be un-filtered |
| `src/signal/event_study.py` | derives the Level 3 → Level 1 crossing from the data and computes the discount path |
| `tests/test_event_study.py` | 8 tests, proving the arithmetic on an injected Level 1 observation |

**Scanned:** every universe company across all 14 quarters on disk, at every fair value level. **10,566 non-Level-3 rows found** — and the breakdown is the finding:

| | rows |
|---|---|
| False positives: the issuer is not the company the pattern claims | **10,126** |
| Right company, wrong instrument (bank debt, 144A, priced per $100 of face) | 186 |
| Genuine equity observations of a universe company | 254 |
| — of those, at **Level 1** | **0** |

**No genuine Level 1 observation of a universe company exists anywhere in the archive.** So the Week 8 conclusion holds, and now it is measured across fourteen quarters rather than inferred from two.

**The surprise is the first row.** Every one of the 7,175 Level 1 rows is **Coherent Corp** — a public company, ticker COHR, caught by the deliberate `%COHERE%` canary planted in Week 4: CFD COHERENT CORP, CFD_EQS FIN LEG COHERENT, COHERENT CORP, COHERENT CORP 07/02/2029. The Level 3 filter had been doing double duty as a *precision* filter, and removing it exposed the frozen name patterns to the entire public market. Any future use of this lane has to route through the matcher and the review queue, not the patterns.

The second row matters too: `X.AI LLC TL 1L BANKDEBT` and `X.AI LLC/X.AI CO ISSUER 144A` are the right company and the wrong instrument, priced near $1.00 because they price per $100 of face value. `plan.md` excludes them by name and the lane has to as well.

**Why the private layer was left alone.** Widening `PRIVATE_FILTER` in place would have been one line, and it would have silently redefined the re-mark rate, the dispersion and the panel — 5,806 rows reconcile against `raw_holdings` as a Level 3 layer. The public lane is a separate table that nothing else reads.

**Three things the harness refuses to do**, each enforced by a test:

1. It does not hardcode an IPO date. The crossing is derived as the first period end at which a company's rows stop being Level 3 and start being Level 1.
2. It does not use `plan.md`'s $236.99. When the filing arrives the number comes from the filing.
3. It benchmarks against the **earliest** Level 1 mark, not the lowest. A later, cheaper quote must not become the reference, because the market moves after an IPO for reasons that have nothing to do with how the private marks were set.

**What unblocks it:** `2026q3_nport.zip is downloaded, built, and scanned with `python -m src.ingest.public_marks 2026q3``. On the chosen route — waiting for the SEC rather than fetching from EDGAR — that is roughly November 2026, once the 2026Q3 filing quarter closes and DERA publishes.

## What none of this shows

- **Marks are not valuations.** Every number here is what a fund wrote down, not what a company is worth. N-PORT gives the fund's share count, never the company's total shares outstanding.
- **Nothing is split-adjusted.** Perplexity's confirmed 10:1 split is excluded from every change calculation above, factor recorded and adjustment not yet applied.
- **Same-date dispersion still mixes disagreement with update timing.** Two managers with the same period end may have last convened their valuation committees weeks apart. The level decomposition narrows this but does not remove it.
- **The propagation lag is bounded below by the reporting stagger**, so it measures observability rather than how fast managers actually work.
